title: Contextual Latency Guardian and Anomaly Smoothing Pipeline
creator: Anjali Rao
description:
Problem: Our current burn-rate and paging alerts are noisy during scheduled traffic shape changes and gradual model rollouts. On-call load is rising because transient latency spikes and degraded downstream caches repeatedly trigger P1 pages even when overall SLOs remain acceptable.

Goal: Build a Contextual Latency Guardian (CLG) — a lightweight inference of request context that feeds an Anomaly Smoothing Pipeline (ASP). CLG+ASP will reduce false-positive burn-rate pages by: 1) tagging traces with rollout/traffic-context, 2) applying probabilistic trace probes and contextual aggregation windows, and 3) feeding a smoothing layer that informs burn-rate calculus and paging decisions.

Scope: engineering changes to tracing hooks (runtime + agent), metrics/log pipeline transformations (Kafka/ingest processors), new dashboard panels (latency composition, context-tagged burn-rate), and a gradual rollout for alert policy moderation (canary groups). This ticket covers design, prototype, and rollout to 10% of production traffic.

Non-goal: Replacing core SLO definitions or changing SLA commitments. Full rollout/perm-policies will be separate follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing hooks instrumented at runtime entry/exit to attach context tags (model_variant, rollout_id, traffic_slice) for >=99% of serviced requests in canary cluster
Anomaly Smoothing Pipeline implemented as a stream transformer that outputs context-tagged latency histograms and a smoothed burn-rate metric to metrics-store (Prometheus+TSDB)
Burn-rate alert rule updated to use smoothed burn-rate and context-based suppressors; false-positive paging rate reduced by >=50% in the 10% canary window compared to baseline
Dashboard panels added: context-tagged p50/p95/p99; burn-rate breakdown by rollout_id and traffic_slice; a noise-index metric for oncall referencing recent suppression events
Runbook updated with guidance for manual override and rollback (how to opt a rollout_id into strict paging)

2026-03-03 - Marcus Li: Spiked a minimal tracing hook change in runtime branch 'clg-spike'. Hook attaches rollout_id if present in request metadata. Performance microbenchmark: ~0.03ms median overhead. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2894
2026-03-05 - Design review (Zoe Kim): Suggested we include 'traffic_slice' (replay vs live) and a low-cardinality 'experiment_group' tag to avoid high-cardinality explosion in metrics-store.

2026-03-07 - Marcus Li: Implemented a sampler for probabilistic trace probes (1% by default, adjustable via config). Added prefilter to drop sensitive attributes before pipeline. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/412

2026-03-09 - Observability SRE (Rafael Ortiz): Validated the ASP transformer prototype that computes sliding-window exponential smoothing over per-context latency histograms. Load test: transformer sustained 200k evts/s on dev cluster with headroom. Dashboard draft: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/CLG-ANOMALY

2026-03-11 - Marcus Li: Added canary rollout plan. Phase A: 10% traffic for 2 weeks with PAGE suppression enabled for contexts marked as rollout_id != 'stable' (suppress if smoothed burn-rate spike dissipates within 5m). Phase B: expand to 50% and runbook review. Plans added to doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/CLG+-+Anomaly+Smoothing+Pipeline
2026-03-12 - Security review request opened: https://security.redwood.ai/reviews/CLG-2026-03-12 (no blocking issues; redaction + encryption checks required).

2026-03-13 - Marcus Li: Canary started at 10% traffic on prod-canary cluster. Early telemetry shows 38% reduction in pages for model rollout contexts in first 24h. Will monitor for next 72h before expanding.
